definition: Paraphrase or paraphrasing in computational linguistics is the natural language processing task of detecting and generating paraphrases.
details: Applications of paraphrasing are varied including information retrieval, question answering, text summarization, and plagiarism detection. Paraphrasing is also useful in the evaluation of machine translation, as well as semantic parsing and generation of new samples to expand existing corpora.

explainer.lead: Paraphrasing is the NLP task of detecting when two texts mean the same thing and generating new text with the same meaning. It underpins retrieval, question answering, summarisation and plagiarism checks, and it supplies extra training data when corpora are small.

tiers.eli5: It is teaching a computer to say the same thing in different words, and to notice when two sentences are just two ways of saying one thing.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use paraphrase detection to score candidate answers against references and paraphrase generation to augment scarce training data. A common pitfall is accepting surface overlap as meaning equivalence, so systems that copy wording score well while true paraphrases are missed.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally the task splits into paraphrase identification, a binary classification over a sentence pair, and paraphrase generation, producing a new string with equivalent meaning. Neither has a single agreed equivalence criterion, so evaluation depends on the benchmark and annotator judgement.

explainer.example: A plagiarism detector flags a submitted sentence as a paraphrase of a source sentence even though few words are shared, because the meaning matches.
